newsitem.title: UK: S&P says, likely to go on watch.
newsitem.headline: S&P says, likely to go on watch.

text.p: A Standard & Poor's analyst told Reuters on Friday that the long-term senior debt ratings for Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan were likely to be put on CreditWatch with negative implications.
The analyst said a final decision had not yet been made but an S&P statement was likely to be made later on Friday.
The comments, from S&P director Adele Archer, come amid a battle between GrandMet, Guinness and French LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA.
Archer said there was an added element of uncertainty to merger plans between Grand Met and Guinness.
"There seems to be a little less certainty that the merger will go through as originally proposed," she said.
Guinness and GrandMet currently have long-term senior debt ratings of A plus, she said. Commercial paper ratings would be unaffected if a CreditWatch announcement were to be made, she said.
Grand Met on Friday said a demerger proposal by LVMH would result in a value loss of 1.5 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) and possibly "significantly more".
Grand Met said its planned 24 billion pound merger with Guinness Plc was "on track" and the timetable unaffected by the LVMH objections.
The GrandMet statement came one day after LVMH Chairman
Bernard Arnault flew back to Paris after meeting with three to four major shareholders in Guinness and Grand Met to reiterate his plans for a three-way merger of the firms.
